label: copy-phase input token n
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L) when the fed-back input token is n, i.e. the model has just emitted n and now reads it back. Zero activation for n during the original phase (in_first=1 steps never fire) and essentially zero for any other input (a handful of tiny f/e activations at the last step). The predicate captures ~100% of activation mass and recall, but only ~60% of copy-phase n inputs fire; no simple variable tested (t, recall_idx, L, to_go, in_count, n_digits, prev_tok class) separated active from inactive cases, so precision is incomplete. Activation rate and mass rise mildly with later recall position (recall_idx 6-8, long L), and top activations (~3.5) are n near the end of 9-token sequences; no other magnitude claims checked.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: n, f, e, -, x, w; least: p, 3, m, <DEL>) and the next token to output (most: k, b, s, m, t, d; least: e, 0, n, f); timing cues that raise it most: L=4 & t=7, L=5 & t=9, recall_idx=7.
